author: product-requirements-expert
title: Narrow the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Either published form of the veterinarian directory can be narrowed to the veterinarians holding one named specialty, matched on the whole name without regard to letter case. The machine-readable form becomes a supported way to read the directory rather than an artifact.
acceptance_criteria: given no specialty is named, when the machine-readable directory is requested, then it carries every veterinarian with their specialties
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when either form of the directory is requested naming it, then only those veterinarians are listed
given that specialty named in a different letter case, when either form is requested, then the same veterinarians are listed
given only part of a specialty's name, when either form is requested, then no veterinarian is listed
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is requested, then the directory comes back with no veterinarian in it and reports no failure
given a specialty named as empty or as spaces alone, when either form is requested, then the directory comes back whole, as when none is named
given a narrowed page directory running to more than one page, when a later page is opened, then the narrowing still holds and the paging counts the narrowed directory
given no specialty is named, when either form is requested, then it behaves as it did before this slice
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or other page control for narrowing — neither form gains one in this request
free-text search over veterinarians, pets, or visits, which NG-9 still declines
narrowing by any veterinarian attribute other than specialty
narrowing any listing other than the veterinarian directory
managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2)
notes: Owner-stated request contract, carried here rather than in the PRD because it is mechanism: both vet list surfaces accept an optional 'specialty' query parameter; page links carry it so narrowed pages stay navigable. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused. The dispatch-start at line 1 mis-stamped the req_id as REQ-VET-004; line 2 supersedes it and REQ-VET-004 is not minted. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-31-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md — that file is outside this agent's write scope.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice follows the project's established shape for narrowing a paged listing: a Spring Data derived query taking the narrowing value and a Pageable, called directly from the controller with no service layer (system-design.md Package Structure; ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). OwnerRepository.findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) is the exact precedent. What is new is how the case-insensitive match is expressed. Durable memory previously recorded case-insensitivity as a schema-level property reached three different ways per vendor, and recorded the PostgreSQL owner-search divergence that resulted. This slice sets the opposite rule for matching and records it: ADR 2026-08-31-case-folding-in-the-query-not-the-schema. A second decision keeps the narrowed reads out of the unbounded vets cache: ADR 2026-08-31-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-vets-cache. system-design.md is updated in three places (Persistence, Contracts rows for Vets/VetRepository/VetController, Known Defects) and docs/adr/README.md gains three index rows.
integration_points: VetRepository gains a narrowed read in two arities, mirroring the existing findAll()/findAll(Pageable) pair: an unpaged Collection<Vet> variant serving the machine-readable route, and a Page<Vet> variant serving the HTML route. Both are derived queries over the specialties association with IgnoreCase, e.g. findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase. Neither carries @Cacheable.

VetController: both handlers gain @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty. Each handler normalizes it through one private static helper in the controller, which trims and maps blank to null. Null selects the existing unnarrowed, cached call; non-null selects the narrowed call. This is the single shared normalization point both surfaces use.
The HTML route puts the normalized specialty into the model so page links can carry it. Page counts come from the returned Page, so totalPages and totalItems already describe the narrowed directory.

The machine-readable route stays unpaged and returns the whole narrowed list in the existing Vets wrapper. Vets.Implements moves from em-dash to REQ-VET-001, REQ-VET-003; the Known Defects row calling that route requirement-less is removed.
vetList.html page links gain the specialty parameter. No form, dropdown, or other page control is added.

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) - the project's pattern for narrowing a paged listing by a caller-supplied value. The narrowing and the paging are one database query, so page counts describe the narrowed set. Follow this rather than filtering the cached collection in memory: in-memory filtering would move paging out of the database and give the HTML surface a second paging mechanism.

the existing findAll() / findAll(Pageable) overload pair - an unpaged Collection variant and a paged Page variant of one query. The narrowed read mirrors this pair rather than passing Pageable.unpaged(), so the machine-readable route's absence of paging stays visible in the type.

page links are currently built by Thymeleaf expression preprocessing on a concatenated string ('/vets.html?page=__${i}__'). Do not extend that form to carry the specialty. Build every page link with the link-expression syntax @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=...)} so Thymeleaf URL-encodes the caller-supplied value.

risks.risk: H2 types specialties.name as plain VARCHAR(80) and PostgreSQL types it TEXT; both compare case-sensitively. Only MySQL folds case by collation. An implementation that relies on collation, or on an exact equality match, fails the ignore-case criterion on two of the three supported vendors.
risks.mitigation: Express the fold in the query: IgnoreCase on the derived query name, which Spring Data JPA emits as UPPER(name) = UPPER(:name). Portable across all three vendors. This is the same trap as the recorded PostgreSQL owner-search defect, and it bites harder here because two vendors are affected instead of one. Recorded in ADR 2026-08-31-case-folding-in-the-query-not-the-schema.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository. Every controller-level test of the ignore-case criterion passes trivially, because the mock never runs a query. The acceptance criterion 'the same veterinarians are listed for a different letter case' cannot be verified at that level.
risks.mitigation: Add repository-level coverage in ClinicServiceTests, which is a @DataJpaTest running against the real H2 schema and seed data (radiology, surgery, dentistry) and already exercises VetRepository.findAll(). Assert there that a differently-cased whole name matches and that a partial name does not. The controller tests then cover routing, model, normalization, and link carry-through.

risks.risk: The narrowing joins a to-many association, so a veterinarian could appear more than once if two specialty rows ever shared a name, which would also corrupt the page counts.
risks.mitigation: Use Distinct in the derived query name, so both the content query and the derived count query deduplicate on the root entity.

risks.risk: The vets cache is declared with statistics only - no eviction and no entry limit, and no JCache provider configuration exists to supply one. Annotating a narrowed read @Cacheable('vets') would key entries on an unauthenticated, attacker-controlled string.
risks.mitigation: Narrowed reads are uncached. The two unnarrowed reads keep @Cacheable('vets') unchanged, so the default path's behavior and performance are untouched. Recorded in ADR 2026-08-31-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-vets-cache.

risks.risk: The specialty value is reflected into href attributes on every page link. String-concatenated or preprocessed link construction would put a caller-supplied value into markup unencoded.
risks.mitigation: Thymeleaf link-expression parameters are URL-encoded, and th:text output is HTML-escaped by default. Both layers hold as long as the links use @{...(param=value)} form. Nothing in this slice renders the specialty as page text.

risks.risk: UPPER(name) does not use the existing index on specialties.name, so the narrowed query scans.
risks.mitigation: Accepted. The seeded specialty list has three rows and the route is not hot. A functional index is a separate decision, noted in the ADR's Consequences.

notes: Product gaps taken at the narrowest reading, per dispatch instruction that no product answer can arrive. (1) A narrowing that matches no veterinarian renders the table with no rows and no message. No empty-state text is added: a page control is a non-goal, no message key exists for it, and 'comes back with no veterinarian in it and reports no failure' is satisfied by an empty table and a 200. (2) Acceptance criterion 'behaves as it did before this slice' is read as the directory contents, the page counts, and the model attributes - not the literal query string of page links. A page link may carry an empty specialty parameter when nothing is narrowed; that round-trips to the whole directory through the same normalization. (3) Normalization is placed in one private static helper on VetController rather than an @InitBinder StringTrimmerEditor. The editor would work and would be shorter, but it hides the 'blank narrows nothing' rule from the handler bodies; explicitness wins here and both routes still share exactly one definition. Design-doc edits are written ahead of the code, as this pipeline expects; doc-sync reconciles after the slice lands. The removed Known Defects row ('the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement') is falsified by REQ-VET-003, which docs/prd.md:176 confirms. docs/adr/README.md gained three index rows: the carried non-goal ADR row plus this slice's two. Autofix audit: the log holds no prd-autofix or design-doc-autofix records; nothing to audit. Out of scope but noted: scripts/doctor.py check reports project-data spec_version 0.1.0 against manifest 0.2.0 in scripts/layout.toml. It pre-dates this slice and is untouched here. It matters only in that the doctor is a blocking gate, so a real structural regression introduced by this slice would surface behind an already-red check - worth clearing in its own slice. Also pre-existing and untouched: /vets.html?page=0 reaches PageRequest.of(-1, 5) and yields a 500; the paged findAll is already @Cacheable on a caller-supplied page number, which is the unbounded-key path these ADRs decline to widen.

findings.description: The cache-bypass mitigation is correct in the code but is asserted nowhere. The ADR (docs/adr/2026-08-31-narrowed-vet-reads-bypass-the-vets-cache.md) rests on the narrowed reads never being @Cacheable("vets"), because that cache is created in CacheConfiguration.java:37-51 with statistics only -- no eviction, no entry limit -- and the specialty is an unauthenticated, attacker-chosen cache key of unbounded cardinality. Verified as written: @Cacheable("vets") appears only on findAll() (VetRepository.java:45) and findAll(Pageable) (VetRepository.java:55), both unchanged; no @Cacheable exists anywhere else in src/main/java; the controller reaches the narrowed reads directly (VetController.java:70, 81) with no intervening cached method. But nothing fails if a later edit adds the annotation for symmetry -- ClinicServiceTests runs under @DataJpaTest where caching is not even active, and VetControllerTests stubs the repository. Contrast the sibling mitigation, reflected input in page links, which IS pinned by thePageLinksShouldEncodeASpecialtyThatLooksLikeMarkup. The security-motivated decision with no regression guard is the only instance of its class in this slice; the encoding decision and the unnarrowed-reads-unchanged claim are both covered.
findings.fix: Add one test pinning the annotation's absence, so reintroducing it fails the build. Reflectively assert both narrowed overloads carry no Cacheable annotation, e.g. assertThat(VetRepository.class.getMethod("findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase", String.class).getAnnotation(org.springframework.cache.annotation.Cacheable.class)).isNull(), and the same for the (String, Pageable) overload. Name it for the rule it defends (a narrowed vet read should not be cached) and reference the ADR in a why-comment.

approved_aspects: No SQL/JPQL injection on the derived-query path: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase is a Spring Data derived query, so the specialty is bound as a JPQL parameter and IgnoreCase folds case as UPPER(:name) in the query. No @Query, no native query, no string concatenation reaches the persistence layer anywhere in the diff.

Reflected input in the five page links is genuinely encoded: the previous __${i}__ expression-preprocessing form is replaced by link-expression parameters @{/vets.html(page=..., specialty=${specialty})}, which URL-encode the value and then HTML-escape the attribute. Swept the whole templates tree for the injection sink -- zero occurrences of __$ and zero of th:utext remain in src/main/resources/templates. The mitigation is asserted: thePageLinksShouldEncodeASpecialtyThatLooksLikeMarkup drives "><script>alert(1)</script> end-to-end and asserts both the percent-encoded form and the absence of a raw <script>.

specialty is a String request parameter, so no binding failure and no type-mismatch path exists on it; a malformed value cannot produce an exception, let alone leak detail. No error-detail exposure is configured or added (no server.error.include-* settings anywhere in src/main).

Trust-boundary handling is single-sourced: narrowingSpecialty (VetController.java:93-95) is the one definition both surfaces use, and blank/whitespace input degrades to the unnarrowed read rather than to an empty-string query. Blank handling is asserted on both surfaces by parameterized tests.

Unbounded result size on the unpaged JSON surface introduces no new class: /vets?specialty=X returns at most the vets holding one specialty, a strict subset of what the pre-existing unpaged /vets already returns.
No hardcoded secrets or credential-like values in the diff; a case-insensitive sweep for password/secret/token/api-key/credential across the change set returns nothing.

Supply chain unchanged: no build file appears in the change set (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only), so no dependency is added, upgraded, or repinned and no new CVE surface is introduced by this slice.

Raising as clarify rather than blocking because the brief itself documents the codebase-wide gap (§ Test Pyramid: 'this codebase does not currently hold it') and does not mandate extracting a rule to package-private/testable scope inside a slice; a human or the brief owner should decide whether this slice's small, easily-isolated rule is the kind meant to close the gap.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: My round-1 finding is resolved. The substituted assertion in VetRepositoryTests.aReadNarrowedByACallerSuppliedSpecialtyShouldNotBeCacheable does defend the rule I named: it fails the build if @Cacheable is placed on either narrowed overload, which is exactly the 'added for symmetry with the findAll pair' reintroduction path the finding described. The structural form is a superset of the two-overload form I proposed, not a weaker substitute -- it also covers a narrowed read added later, which the explicit form would have silently missed.

Non-vacuity is genuinely guarded. VetRepository extends Repository<Vet, Integer>, a marker interface with no methods, and getMethods() on an interface does not surface java.lang.Object methods, so the filtered collection is exactly the two narrowed overloads today. isNotEmpty() therefore fails if a rename or signature change empties the filter, which is the failure mode that would otherwise turn allSatisfy into a vacuous pass. Verified by running ./gradlew test --tests '*VetRepositoryTests*': green.

Revert claim verified independently, not taken on report. git hash-object on the working-tree VetRepository.java and git rev-parse on the same path in the round-1 basis tree d4cbcc4 both yield blob 98a5958, so the file is byte-identical to the state I reviewed in round 1. git diff against that tree for VetRepository.java, VetController.java, and templates/vets/vetList.html is empty. The @Cacheable plant left no residue.

The String-parameter proxy is sound in the direction that matters and fails safe in the other. False-negative direction (the real residual gap): a future narrowed read whose narrowing argument is not a String -- findDistinctBySpecialtiesIn(Collection<String>) (erased to Collection), findBySpecialtiesId(Integer), an enum or wrapper specialty type, or a Specification/Example argument -- would be caller-narrowed yet skipped by the filter, so caching it would pass. False-positive direction: an unnarrowed read that happens to take a String would be caught and refused caching. That direction is over-restrictive rather than permissive, and it forces a human to look at the Javadoc's stated convention before proceeding, so it cannot silently weaken the mitigation. Net posture is strictly better than round 1, where no guard existed at all.

Two narrower reintroduction paths the annotation check does not cover, recorded for the audit trail rather than as a defect: a type-level @Cacheable on the VetRepository interface (getAnnotation is read per-method, and Spring applies a type-level @Cacheable to all methods), and a custom annotation meta-annotated with @Cacheable (getAnnotation does not resolve meta-annotations, unlike AnnotatedElementUtils). Both are exotic relative to the per-method copy-paste this codebase's existing style invites, and neither is a regression introduced by this slice. Not raising them as findings: they are defense-in-depth on a test-only guard, and the Javadoc states the structural convention plainly enough that a cold reader sees what the check does and does not mean.

Fix delta is test and prose only. scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree d4cbcc4 --name-only lists exactly two paths: the new test class and one ADR sentence split (the doc-reviewer's writing-standards autofix, no change of meaning to the cache rationale). No production Java, no template, no build file, no configuration file moved.

Nothing else in the slice's security posture moved. Re-swept src/main/java for Cacheable/CachePut/Caching: @Cacheable("vets") appears only on findAll() (line 45) and findAll(Pageable) (line 55), both unchanged; the only other hit is @EnableCaching in CacheConfiguration. The round-1 approvals stand unchanged -- derived-query parameter binding with no @Query or string concatenation, the link-expression encoding of the reflected specialty in the page links, single-sourced blank normalization in narrowingSpecialty, and no secrets in the diff.

Supply chain unchanged for this pass. No build.gradle, gradle/, properties, or yml file appears in the fix delta, so no dependency was added, upgraded, or repinned and no new CVE surface was introduced since the round-1 check.

The new test file is plain JUnit in the vet package rather than @DataJpaTest, which is the right choice for this guard: the assertion is about a declared annotation, so booting a context or a database would add startup cost without adding signal, and a @DataJpaTest slice does not activate caching anyway -- which is precisely why the existing ClinicServiceTests could never have caught the regression.

author: change-grader
summary: narrow the vet directory by specialty on both surfaces

blast_radius.note: Reach is one bounded context: 81 production lines across VetRepository, VetController, and the vetList template, all inside the vet package that nothing else depends on. The 43 hunks and 12 files are inflated by three new ADRs and PRD/system-design prose; no sensitive path is touched, and scripts/layout.toml with its known doctor spec_version mismatch is outside the diff entirely. The one pre-existing surface disturbed is the unnarrowed vet-list page links, which the template rewrite converts from string-preprocessed hrefs to parameterized link expressions.

semantic_surprise.note: I read every production hunk for behavior the diff size would not predict and found none. The unnarrowed paths are byte-preserved: findAll() and findAll(Pageable) keep their cache annotation, and both handlers fall through to them whenever narrowingSpecialty returns null, so absent, empty, and whitespace-only specialties answer with the whole directory exactly as before. The narrowed reads are Spring Data derived queries with bound parameters, so the unauthenticated specialty text cannot reach SQL as syntax, and they are deliberately uncached against an unbounded, unevicted vets cache. The specialty reaches the template only as a link parameter, never as printed text, so it is URL-encoded rather than interpolated. The one detail no test pins is whether an unnarrowed page link now renders a trailing empty specialty parameter, and it is inert by construction: blank narrows nothing on both surfaces, and that rule is directly tested.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behavior rather than restating it, and several would fail against a plausibly broken implementation. Query semantics run against real H2 under DataJpaTest with adversarial fixtures: a mixed-case spelling the seed data never uses, a prefix that whole-name matching must reject, an unheld specialty, and a distinct-plus-paging case asserting content size, total elements, and total pages together. The MockMvc tests cover both surfaces for narrowed, empty, blank, and absent specialties, carry the narrowing across pages with a stub that really slices by the requested Pageable, and assert both that a markup-like specialty appears percent-encoded and that no raw script tag appears. The reflection test defending the cache bypass carries a non-empty guard, so it cannot pass vacuously. The gap is small: narrowingSpecialty has no direct unit test and trimming a padded non-blank value is covered only indirectly.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round two is four approvals from the full dispatched roster with zero findings between them, and the approvals rest on independent verification rather than report: the query plan was read from the build log, the reverted file was checked by hash, and the reflection test was run in isolation. Round one was a working gate, not a hedge: the security reviewer's changes_requested named a real unasserted mitigation, and its own re-review calls the implementer's substituted structural assertion a superset of what it proposed. The one surviving round-one finding is a clarify routed to the brief owner about unit-testing a pure helper, explicitly disclaimed as not a defect, and not repeated in round two.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the triaged surface and honors all three product decisions. NG-9 is narrowed to free-text search rather than dropped, with its own non-goal ADR; the JSON route is reinstated under REQ-VET-003 while the superseded entry states the withdrawn REQ-VET-002 id is not reused; and the template gains no form, select, or input, only specialty-carrying page links, so the filter stays a URL contract. The single design revision is bookkeeping rather than drift, since the superseding design-block exists to bring the three ADR files under a design record after the autofix audit aborted the gate, and no code changed for it. Build retries and consultations are zero.

rationale: Small, contained, and behaviorally conservative: the unnarrowed paths are unchanged and still cached, the narrowed reads are parameterized and deliberately uncached, and the specialty reaches the page only URL-encoded. Confirm and merge. The two open questions are recorded product deferrals, not gaps.
